messages:
Bryce (PM): Quick sync — post-launch follow-ups. We have: 1) customer hotpath latency spike at tail (p95 up 120ms), 2) UX edit flow request (smaller scope), 3) QA flagged intermittent mem growth on dedicated. Need to decide bug vs enhancement for next sprint. Thoughts?
Leah (Eng): Can you paste the telemetry links? I want to see distribution by model/seq len.
Bryce (PM): https://go/dashboard/infra/1234 — p95 by route. Most spikes on /generate-chat when seq > 512. Customer A reports during multi-turn chats.
Devon (Eng): If it's sequence-length correlated, quick win might be batching config + KV cache tuning. That would be a config change (enhancement) but could be rolled fast. Risk: might not fix memory growth.
Sara (CS): From the customer side: they're asking for reduced tail latency first — they're ok with a config change if it gives immediate improvement. They flagged the memory issue separately and want a plan.
Carter (SRE): Memory growth repro from QA looks like a leak in the runtime's KV cache eviction under bursty traffic. Lab logs attached.
QA Bot: repro snippet:
```
curl -X POST https://dedicated.api/redwood -d '{"route":"/generate-chat","seq_len":1024}'
# after 10k requests resident set increases ~30MB
```
Leah (Eng): That snippet helps. If eviction isn't firing at the right thresholds, prioritise that as a bug. Fix path: change eviction watermark + add metrics around cache retention. ETA: 1 sprint for hotfix + 2-day canary.
Devon (Eng): UX edit flow (customer asks) is smaller, estimated 3 days. It's an enhancement but high perceived value. Recommend we put it in the 'follow-on' bucket with a canary.
Bryce (PM): Proposal: Sprint next — prioritize: 1) KV eviction fix (bug) — critical for Dedicated customers, 2) latency config tuning (enhancement but quick; ship in same sprint), 3) UX edit flow (enhancement) — schedule for following sprint unless we can bundle.
Sara (CS): Customer A approves prioritising KV fix + config. They want weekly updates. I'll set expectation.
Carter (SRE): Also recommend enabling additional tracing for the canary: add route-level memory metrics and an alert if RSS growth > 50MB in 5m.
Leah (Eng): I'll open two PRs: eviction fix (target: patch release), and telemetry for canary. Devon will own the config tuning PR. Plan to ship patch in 1.5 weeks.
Devon (Eng): I'll put up a minimal config toggle: continuous batching throttles and kv_cache_size_override. Sample config:
```
{ "kv_cache_size": "dynamic", "batch_max_tokens": 256 }
```
Bryce (PM): OK — next steps: Leah/Devon implement, Carter runs canary, Sara keeps customer updated. Backlog: add a ticket for UX edit flow with acceptance criteria from Sara. I'll create the sprint tickets after this thread. :thumbsup:
Sara (CS): Thanks — please cc me when tickets are created.
QA Bot: Test plan queued for canary: smoke + 24h leak monitor.
Bryce (PM): If anything slips, escalate here. Closing the thread once tickets exist.
Leah (Eng): Created ticket RED-3421 (eviction fix) and RED-3422 (telemetry + canary). Links shared in sprint board.
Bryce (PM): Added RED-3423 for UX edit flow (ACs from Sara + mockups). Scheduling for next sprint backlog grooming.
Sara (CS): Confirmed. :eyes: 
Carter (SRE): I'll schedule the canary for Tue 09:00 PT. Will post results.
Bryce (PM): Thanks everyone — I'll follow up in the sprint planning meeting.
